A developer needs to enable the GraphQL IDE to run test queries against the Experience Edge schema. What must be configured?
Enable the GraphQL Playground item in the CM content tree
VERIFIED ✓ Sitecore_GraphQL_ExposePlayground=true enables the built-in GraphQL IDE for testing Experience Edge schema queries.
A developer receives an error "Authorization error" when calling the Sitecore GraphQL API. What is the most likely cause?
The API key header (sc_apikey) is invalid or missing
The GraphQL query syntax is wrong
VERIFIED ✓ Authorization errors on Sitecore GraphQL API are typically caused by missing/invalid sc_apikey header.
A developer creates a new data template and notices it is NOT available in the Experience Edge GraphQL schema after publishing. What is the most likely cause?
The template must be explicitly registered via the Experience Edge Admin API
The template was not placed in an approved folder path (Project, Feature, Foundation, or User Defined)
Experience Edge schema needs manual regeneration
VERIFIED ✓ Templates must reside in /sitecore/templates/Project, /Feature, /Foundation, or /User Defined to appear in the Experience Edge GraphQL schema. (Sitecore Edge docs.)
Which statement BEST differentiates Sitecore AI CMS Components from Headless SXA Components?
AI CMS Components require code; Headless SXA are no-code
AI CMS Components are a low-code/no-code visual builder for components consuming multiple data sources; Headless SXA Components require developer code and consume data from the same data source
AI CMS Components are only for static content
Headless SXA components use React; AI CMS Components use Angular

VERIFIED ✓ Sitecore AI CMS Components = low/no-code visual builder consuming multiple data sources; Headless SXA = requires developer code from the same data source. (Multiple dump sources agree on B.)
A developer needs to allow content authors to apply custom CSS styles to a component directly from the Pages editor. What is the required step?
Create a custom rendering variant for each style
Add the IStyling base template to the component's rendering parameters template
Add a CSS field to the component's datasource template
Enable the Style Library in sitecore.json
VERIFIED ✓ IStyling base template located at /sitecore/templates/Foundation/Experience Accelerator/Presentation/Rendering Parameters/IStyling. Exposes Styles dropdown in Page Builder.
A developer wants to create a new component to display content from a data source. What are the optimal steps?
Create the new component in Next.js and export it to Sitecore via CLI
Create or reuse an SXA Module, insert a new rendering, use the JSS CLI to scaffold a new component
Create or reuse an SXA Module, clone an existing component that uses a data source, create the React component based on the cloned one
Create or reuse an SXA Module, clone a component, create the React component based on the original
VERIFIED ✓ Cloning an existing component that uses a data source is the recommended SXA pattern per Sitecore Accelerate Cookbook and official 'Build your first component' docs.
A developer wants to deploy to SitecoreAI CMS but is NOT using a source code provider with an out-of-the-box connector. How can they deploy?
Develop a custom connector for the Deploy app
Use the Sitecore Cloud CLI with scripting to automate deployment
Use Vercel as an intermediary platform
VERIFIED ✓ Sitecore Cloud CLI is the documented approach for non-standard source code providers (no out-of-the-box connector).
A Sitecore architect needs to move a project to a new repository. What are the recommended steps?
Delete the existing project in the Deploy app and recreate
Modify local Git config to point to new repo — Sitecore auto-updates
Edit the project in the Deploy app, update repository details and branch per environment, then manually create a build and deploy
Export via SCS package and import to new repo
VERIFIED ✓ Recommended: edit the project in the XM Cloud Deploy app, update repo details and branch per environment, then create a manual build.
A front-end developer is building a component to display content from Sitecore AI CMS that must support Page Builder authoring. Which approach is most appropriate?
Directly query the Delivery API with fetch() and render with HTML elements
Create a static component with hardcoded content
Use Content SDK Node helper components to render the data, ensuring compatibility with Page Builder
Fetch layout data directly from the Sitecore database
VERIFIED ✓ Content SDK field helper components (Text, Image, RichText, Link) are required for Page Builder inline editing compatibility.
In the Content Editor, an administrator-level user cannot see the Layouts or Templates nodes. Which of the following would explain the missing nodes?
The user's account has been locked
The user needs to enable "Hidden items" on the View tab to reveal system nodes
The nodes require a workflow state to be visible
VERIFIED ✓ 'Hidden items' checkbox on the View tab (Content Editor) reveals system nodes including Layouts and Templates.
A developer is updating security access rights for a new role in the Security Editor. Which of the following permissions are they able to manage? (Select all that apply)
VERIFIED ✓ Manageable rights in Security Editor: Read, Write, Create, Delete, Rename, Admin + Inheritance. 'Debug' and 'Access' are NOT real Sitecore access rights.

Which of the following tasks are performed by the publishing pipeline to create an accurate snapshot of the content available for publishing from the Content Management instance? (Select all that apply)
VERIFIED ✓ The publishing pipeline performs: calculating dependencies, resolving dependencies, and calculating additional entities. 'Archiving expired content' is NOT a publishing pipeline task.

A team is working on a SitecoreAI CMS project. Each developer has their own local environment connected to a shared CMS instance. Which is the most efficient practice they should follow regarding VCS branches and environment configurations?
Each developer creates feature branches, ensures local .env variables match the remote CMS context for their branch, and tests locally before merging
Designate one developer to manage all merges while others commit locally only
All developers work on main branch continuously pushing changes
Regenerate Context ID before each branch or code change
VERIFIED ✓ Per Sitecore developer best practices, feature branches with matching .env context variables tested locally before merge is the recommended workflow.
A frontend developer needs to display a list of items selected from a multilist field. Which approach is most appropriate to render the selected items?
Access the field value directly — it returns a JSON string of values
Access the field value.value property which contains an HTML structure
Access the field value property, which contains an array of item IDs, then loop through them to render using the Delivery API
Allow components to execute the search and return all matching items
VERIFIED ✓ Multilist field value returns an array of item reference IDs in Content SDK/JSS; developers loop through and render each via Delivery API or field helpers.
A team is considering the Front-End First (FEF) development approach for a SitecoreAI CMS project. Which statement best explains why FEF is generally the preferred approach?
FEF enables developers to connect to the CMS preview endpoint, allowing workstreams to progress with completely distinct development rows
FEF allows developers to build components using only mock data initially, reducing dependency on SitecoreAI CMS until the final integration stage
FEF ensures teams can work entirely offline, eliminating the need for Sitecore Cloud Portal authentication
FEF provides greater compatibility with traditional Sitecore modules by simulating a full CM environment
VERIFIED ✓ Front-End First (FEF) decouples frontend development from CMS availability via mock data, enabling parallel workstreams until final integration.

An organization needs to automate the creation of SitecoreAI CMS environments as part of their CI/CD pipelines without direct access to the Cloud Portal UI. Which approach provides the most flexible automated solution?
Use the Sitecore Cloud CLI or REST API to automate environment creation, allowing scripting and CI/CD pipeline integration
Environments are automatically created during deployment — no explicit creation needed
Developers create and configure each environment through the Deploy app UI
Define environment configs in .env files and trigger creation by re-deploying the application
VERIFIED ✓ Sitecore Cloud CLI and REST API support programmatic environment creation, enabling CI/CD automation without UI access.
A developer needs to log in to the SitecoreAI Deploy app to create a project using a starter template but lacks the required permissions. What needs to happen?
An Organization Admin or Organization Owner must update the developer's role in the Sitecore Cloud Portal
An Organization Admin or Organization Owner must update the role using the SitecoreAI Deploy app
Only the Organization Owner can update roles, using the Deploy app
Only the Organization Owner can update roles, using the Cloud Portal
VERIFIED ✓ Role updates for Deploy app access are performed by an Organization Admin or Owner in the Sitecore Cloud Portal — not within the Deploy app itself.
A SitecoreAI CMS build process has failed. Which option provides the most direct and comprehensive information to diagnose the error?
The overall system status page of the Deploy app indicating platform health
The deployment log files for the environment, accessible via the SitecoreAI Deploy app
The rendering host logs accessible via the environment detail page
The SCS module deployment status in the environment
VERIFIED ✓ Deployment log files in the Sitecore Deploy app provide the most granular, actionable information for build failure diagnosis.
A development team is diagnosing intermittent deployment failures in a SitecoreAI CMS environment. Which approach yields the most granular and actionable insights?
Review the detailed deployment log, focusing on provisioning, build, deployment, and post-action stages, to pinpoint error messages
Examine CM instance logs for content-related issues such as serialization errors
Monitor real-time network traffic and server resource utilization
Aggregate high-level metrics from the Deploy app system status page
VERIFIED ✓ The detailed deployment log (provisioning → build → deployment → post-action stages) is the recommended approach for diagnosing intermittent pipeline failures.
A developer needs to completely clear the Experience Edge cache to resolve a publishing layout issue. How can they do this?
Go to the Sitecore Content Editor and publish the entire site
Use the Experience Edge Admin API to clear the cache for the tenant
Use the Experience Edge Admin API to clear the cache (POST /v1/caches/clear)
Submit a support ticket to restart the Experience Edge tenant

VERIFIED ✓ Experience Edge Admin API clears the CDN delivery cache. Note: Options B and C are both technically correct (both invoke the Admin API); option C is more specific (POST /v1/caches/clear). Pass4success community consensus marks the 'for the tenant' phrasing as the cleanest match — either B or C is accepted.
Which Sitecore Content Serialization CLI command does a developer run to push changes made within a developer-managed codebase (i.e., establish an authenticated connection before pushing)?
VERIFIED ✓ 'dotnet sitecore connect' establishes an authenticated connection to the target Sitecore environment before serialization operations.
What Sitecore Content Serialization command can a developer run to automatically ensure changes made in the CMS are written to disk and tracked in source control?
VERIFIED ✓ 'dotnet sitecore ser watch' monitors the local Sitecore instance and auto-serializes item changes to disk in real time.
A developer wants to limit serialization of items under a Navigation item to just the item itself and one level below. What property should they add to the inclusion?
Nothing — this is the default behavior
VERIFIED ✓ The 'scope' property in SCS module config controls serialization depth (SingleItem / ItemAndChildren / ItemAndDescendants / DescendantsOnly).

A developer is building a component that supports multiple layout options for the same content (Image left, Image right, Image centered — each with title and CTA). The solution must allow authors to reuse the same content across all layout variations. Which approach best meets these requirements?
Create a single component and expose rendering parameters for layout toggle
Create one component with three headless variants, each handling a different layout

Which security practice must developers follow when dealing with authentication in Sitecore XM Cloud?
Use a single shared admin account to simplify developer access
Store authentication credentials locally in public Git repositories
Use API keys and authentication tokens instead of hardcoding credentials in code

A developer needs to optimize a slow-loading product catalog page. They suspect inefficient GraphQL queries. Which strategy best improves performance with the Experience Edge GraphQL API?

Request all available fields in a single comprehensive query to minimize round-trips
Disable caching at the Experience Edge level to ensure up-to-date content

A developer wants to invite a team member to their Sitecore Cloud Portal organization and give them access to the apps inside. What role should they assign?

What is the execution policy file in a local environment configuration for a containerized Sitecore development stack?
The environment variables file (.env) for Sitecore Docker deployment
A custom configuration file defining variables for headless environments
The configuration file for the Sitecore development tooling

What is the purpose of the sitecore.json file in a Sitecore development solution?
The environment variables file for the Sitecore Docker deployment
A custom configuration file defining a solution for headless environments
The configuration file for the Sitecore development tooling
The solution integration file needed for deploying code changes
